title: Case Registered Against Former Madurai Deputy Mayor Mannan Over TVK Horse-Trading Claim
excerpt: Based on Madurai Central MLA V.M.S. Mustafa's complaint, the Central Crime Branch booked former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan under the Prevention of Corruption Act and for criminal conspiracy, and picked him up for inquiry.
body:
• Chennai's Central Crime Branch has registered a case against former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan, now with the AIADMK, based on Madurai Central TVK MLA V.M.S. Mustafa's complaint of a horse-trading bid, The Hindu reported.
  • The case was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and for criminal conspiracy, and Mannan was picked up for inquiry, according to the report.
  • Mustafa alleged on November 4 that he was offered Rs 15 crore to support a possible no-confidence motion, and said both the AIADMK and the DMK were involved in attempts to lure TVK legislators.
  • The allegation follows an earlier case in July, when three men were arrested after another TVK MLA said he was offered Rs 35 crore to influence his vote on a resolution against the Assembly Speaker.

Police in Tamil Nadu have registered a case against former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan after Madurai Central MLA V.M.S. Mustafa of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) complained of a bid to buy his support, The Hindu reported. The Central Crime Branch (CCB) registered the case under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and for criminal conspiracy, and Mannan, who is now with the AIADMK, was picked up for inquiry.

What Mustafa alleged

Mustafa first made the allegation publicly on Tuesday, November 4, speaking to reporters at Madurai Airport after arriving from Chennai. He said he had personally received a phone call offering him Rs 15 crore to support a no-confidence motion whenever it was moved, according to ANI's report of his remarks.

"There are once again attempts to lure TVK legislators through horse-trading. I personally received a phone call offering me Rs 15 crore to support a no-confidence motion whenever it is moved. I have informed the party leadership about this."

— V.M.S. Mustafa, TVK MLA for Madurai Central

Mustafa said AIADMK functionaries from the region had become active after a case was registered against former minister V. Senthil Balaji, and that they were contacting him and attempting to lure legislators. He added that both the AIADMK and the DMK were involved in the attempts, that he had brought the matter to the party leadership's attention, and that even an offer of Rs 100 crore would not make TVK MLAs switch sides.

A row with cases on both sides

The horse-trading dispute in Tamil Nadu predates Mustafa's complaint. In July, TVK MLA N. Elaiyaraja claimed he was offered Rs 35 crore and threatened to influence his vote in a proposed resolution against the Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. Police registered a case at the D1 Triplicane Police Station in Chennai and arrested three men — Thirunavukkarasu of Arumbakkam, Naresh of Tiruchirappalli and Thiyagarajan of Medavakkam — officials said at the time, according to ANI reporting carried by Web India 123.

The opposition has made counter-allegations of its own. AIADMK Rajya Sabha MP Inbadurai petitioned the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police in July seeking an investigation into alleged horse-trading involving the TVK itself, saying an earlier complaint to the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption, filed on May 30, had drawn no action. The competing claims mean the police are now handling corruption allegations traded between the ruling party and the opposition, rather than a single complaint.

What happens next

The immediate question is what the CCB's inquiry of Mannan produces: whether police treat Mustafa's complaint as a standalone bribery attempt, as part of the wider pattern alleged since July, or as a claim they cannot substantiate. Mustafa said earlier this week that the identities of those behind the attempts would come to light within a day or two. No response from Mannan or the AIADMK to the registration of this case was included in the reports read for this article.
nri_angle: The case is the latest turn in Tamil Nadu's running horse-trading row between the ruling TVK and the AIADMK-DMK opposition, a fight diaspora readers with roots in the state are following closely.
author: Diaspora Desk
